podcast_a1_ep1_cafe.text: Welcome to TalkStage English Podcasts for A1 Beginners. Episode 1: The Morning Cafe. Listen carefully and practice ordering drinks and food.
Good morning! Welcome to Green Bean Cafe. How are you doing today?
Good morning! I am doing well, thank you. It is a lovely sunny day.
It really is! What can I get started for you this morning?
Hmm, let me see. Could I please have a large latte with oat milk?
Of course! A large oat milk latte. Would you like that hot or iced?
Hot, please. And do you have any fresh bakery items today?
Yes, we just baked butter croissants, chocolate muffins, and blueberry scones about ten minutes ago.
Oh, the butter croissant smells wonderful! I will take one croissant, please.
Excellent choice. Would you like me to warm it up for you?
Yes, please. That would be lovely. How much is the total?
That comes to seven dollars and fifty cents. Are you paying with cash or card?
I will pay with credit card, please. Here is my card.
Thank you. You can just tap it right on the screen... Perfect, it went through!
Great! Do you have free Wi-Fi here? I need to do a little bit of study on my laptop.
Yes, we do! The network name is Green Bean Guest, and the password is printed at the bottom of your receipt.
That is very helpful. Is there a table near a power outlet?
Yes, the corner table by the window has two power sockets. It is very quiet and comfortable over there.
Thank you so much! You are very kind.
You are very welcome! Here is your hot oat latte and your warm croissant. Enjoy your breakfast and have a productive study session!
Thank you Liam! Have a fantastic day, see you next time!
See you tomorrow, Emma! Take care!
You have finished Episode 1. Great job on practicing cafe English!

podcast_a1_ep2_routines.text: Welcome to Episode 2: Morning Alarm and Daily Routines. Learn how to describe your everyday schedule, tell the time, and discuss morning habits.
Good morning, David! You look very energetic today. What time do you usually wake up?
Good morning, Sarah! I always wake up at six thirty in the morning. My alarm rings, and I get out of bed immediately.
Six thirty? That is quite early! What is the first thing you do after waking up?
First, I drink a large glass of warm water. Then, I brush my teeth, take a quick shower, and put on my clothes.
Do you usually eat breakfast at home or on the way to work?
I always eat breakfast at home. I make scrambled eggs, whole wheat toast, and a cup of black coffee. What about you, Sarah? What is your morning routine?
My routine is a little different. I wake up at seven fifteen. I do ten minutes of morning yoga and meditation. After that, I eat a bowl of oatmeal with fresh strawberries and honey.
Yoga in the morning sounds very peaceful! How do you travel to your office?
I usually take the subway. The station is only five minutes from my apartment, and the train ride takes about twenty minutes. How do you commute?
When the weather is sunny, I ride my bicycle. When it rains, I take the bus. Cycling gives me fresh air and good exercise before work.
Riding a bicycle to work is fantastic. What time does your workday start?
My work starts at nine o'clock sharp and finishes at five thirty in the evening. In the evening, I cook dinner and read a book.
That sounds like a very healthy and balanced daily routine, David!
Thank you, Sarah! Consistency is key to a happy day.
Episode 2 is complete. Notice the adverbs of frequency: always, usually, and sometimes.

podcast_a1_ep3_city.text: Welcome to Episode 3: Lost in the City. Learn how to politely stop someone on the street, ask for directions, and find landmarks.
Excuse me, hello! I am sorry to bother you, but I am a little lost. Could you help me, please?
Hello! Sure, no problem at all. Where are you trying to go?
I am looking for the Central Metro Station. Is it far from here?
No, it is not far at all. It is only about a seven-minute walk from here.
That is great news! How do I get there from this corner?
Walk straight down this main street for two blocks. When you see a big blue pharmacy on your right, turn left onto Grand Avenue.
Okay, walk straight for two blocks, then turn left at the blue pharmacy. Got it!
Exactly. After you turn left, walk past the city park. The metro station entrance is right opposite the public library. You will see a large yellow M sign.
Is the library next to the park?
Yes, the library is right across the street from the park fountain. You cannot miss it.
Also, is there a ticket machine inside the station, or do I need to buy a card beforehand?
There are automatic ticket machines right at the entrance. They accept both credit cards and cash, and there is an English language option on the screen.
Thank you so much! You saved my day.
You are very welcome! Have a wonderful time exploring our city!
Thank you! Have a great afternoon!
Episode 3 is complete. Remember these key direction phrases: walk straight, turn left, and across the street.

podcast_a1_ep4_restaurant.text: Welcome to Episode 4: Dinner at the Bistro. Practice ordering meals, asking about ingredients, and requesting the bill in English.
Good evening! Welcome to Bella Vista Bistro. Do you have a reservation tonight?
Good evening! Yes, I have a reservation under the name Chloe for two people at seven thirty.
Ah yes, right this way Chloe. I have a lovely quiet table for you next to the garden terrace.
This table is wonderful, thank you so much.
Here are your menus. Can I start you off with something to drink while you look over the food?
Yes, please. Could we have a bottle of sparkling mineral water with lemon slices?
Certainly, sparkling water with lemon. I will be right back with your drinks.
Here is your chilled water. Are you ready to order your main courses, or do you need a few more minutes?
We are ready to order! For the starter, we would like the tomato bruschetta with olive oil.
Excellent. And for your main courses?
I would like the grilled salmon with roasted potatoes and steamed asparagus. Does the salmon come with garlic sauce?
Yes, it comes with a light lemon garlic sauce on the side.
That sounds delicious! And my friend would like the vegetarian mushroom risotto.
Perfect! One grilled salmon and one mushroom risotto. I will place your order with the chef right away.
Thank you very much!
How was everything tonight? Did you enjoy your dinner?
The food was absolutely delicious! Could we please have the bill?
Of course, here is the bill whenever you are ready. Thank you for dining with us tonight!
Thank you Marco! Have a wonderful evening!
Episode 4 is complete. You now know how to order food with confidence!

podcast_a1_ep5_weekend.text: Welcome to Episode 5: Weekend Escapes and Past Memories. Practice talking about what you did yesterday using past tense was, were, and simple past verbs.
Hey Sophie! Happy Friday! How was your week?
Hey Leo! My week was quite busy, but yesterday was very relaxing. Where were you yesterday afternoon?
Yesterday afternoon, I was at the botanical garden. The weather was warm and sunny, so I walked around the rose garden for two hours.
That sounds so peaceful! Did you take any photos?
Yes, I took many photos of the flowers and the lake. What did you do yesterday evening?
Yesterday evening, I stayed home. I cooked vegetable soup, watched a comedy movie on TV, and listened to relaxing music.
That sounds cozy! Do you have any plans for this coming weekend?
Tomorrow, on Saturday, I want to go for a picnic in the Central Park. The weather forecast says it will be twenty-five degrees with no rain.
A picnic in the park is a great idea! Would you like some company? I can bring fresh fruit, cheese, and lemonade.
I would love that! I will prepare homemade turkey sandwiches and bake some chocolate chip cookies tonight.
Yum! Homemade cookies! What time should we meet at the park entrance?
Let's meet at eleven o'clock near the big oak tree by the pond.
Eleven o'clock sounds perfect. I will bring a big picnic blanket and a Frisbee to play after lunch.
Awesome! I am really looking forward to tomorrow, Leo. See you at eleven!
See you tomorrow morning Sophie! Have a great Friday evening!
Congratulations! You have completed all 5 A1 Beginner Masterclass episodes. Keep listening and repeating to master conversational English!
